discovery: Conception and construction of the ATLAS and CMS general-purpose detectors at the LHC, which enabled the discovery of the Higgs boson
motivation: The 2013 Prize recognized the theoretical prediction of the Higgs mechanism, but the experimental achievement that confirmed it has not been honored. Peter Jenni (ATLAS) and Michel Della Negra and Tejinder Virdee (CMS) conceived these detectors in the late 1980s and led their design and construction. Both were built to meet unprecedented demands: 40 MHz bunch crossings, radiation-hard precision tracking, high-resolution calorimetry, large muon spectrometers and multi-level trigger systems that select rare events in real time. Their conceptual choices, including the ATLAS air-core toroids and CMS's compact high-field solenoid with PbWO4 crystal calorimeter, made the 2012 Higgs discovery possible in both the diphoton and four-lepton channels. The detectors now drive precision electroweak and Higgs measurements, rare-process observations and dark-matter searches. This is a qualitative leap in instrumentation that opened a new experimental window on the electroweak scale.
